column1: # Ontology-name → plain-English label projection — the LEXICALIZATION leg of the
# NLG realization stage (Reiter & Dale 2000, *Building Natural Language
# Generation Systems*, CUP: lexicalization is choosing the surface words for a
# domain entity). The "Why?" layer (pragmatics::realize::realize_why) fills its
# {sources} slot from the loaded ontologies a turn reasoned over — each carried
# as a raw internal OntologyName (`caregiving_lexicon`, `usc_title_42`, …). This
# table projects each such name to the human-facing surface a reader can
# understand, so a snake_case internal identifier NEVER leaks into a
# user-facing sentence (the jargon-leak the why-layer critique forbids).
# A name absent from this table is NOT an error: it is projected to the generic
# fallback "your loaded documents" (realize::ontology_labels::plain_label), the
# honest default for any source the engine can load at runtime but this table
# does not name individually. So the projection is total over every possible
# OntologyName without ever emitting a raw identifier.
# Each label names the source as a reader would recognize it — the built-in
# lexicons/bases by what they cover, the U.S. Code titles by their official
# title name (1 U.S.C. § 204; the LRC's USLM catalogue). Sourced from the
# registered entries' own descriptions in praxis.toml.
# Format: `ontology_name<TAB>label`. The `ontology_name` is the registered
# OntologyName as it appears in reasoned_over (praxis.toml `[sources.*]` key, or
# the embedded-base name `LegalSources`); `label` is the plain surface.
# Cite: Reiter & Dale (2000), the realization/lexicalization stage.
